teams.heading: Fiji defeat Canada in Osaka to reach Pacific Nations Cup final
teams.body: The defending champions booked their place in the Pacific Nations Cup final after defeating Canada in Osaka. Ahead of the clash, Canada head coach Stephen Meehan noted that many of Fiji's premier stars were missing due to professional club commitments. However, the Flying Fijians' trademark physical, free-spirited style proved too much for the Canadians. Fiji now progress to the final in Tokyo next weekend, where they will face either Japan or the United States.

lead.why: Fiji's semi-final victory over Canada to reach the Pacific Nations Cup final is the most significant men's international story of the day.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs accuses RFU of having 'blinkers on' over Steve Borthwick backing
teams.body: Former England scrum-half Ben Youngs has criticised Rugby Football Union bosses Conor O'Shea and Bill Sweeney, claiming they have "blinkers on" by extending Steve Borthwick's contract. The head coach is set to sign a deal running until the end of the 2028 Six Nations to avoid World Cup campaign uncertainty. Youngs questioned the decision following England's recent struggles, pointing to Borthwick's win rate of just 59.6% since taking over. O'Shea defended the move, explaining, "You don't want them looking for a job going into [a World Cup]."

teams.heading: World Rugby urges France to support staging Six Nations matches in America
teams.body: World Rugby is intensifying calls for Six Nations unions to relocate flagship games to the United States to help expand the sport's global footprint. Despite the ongoing push from World Rugby, there has been no confirmation from the FFR regarding France's willingness to forfeit a home gate for an American venue.

teams.heading: IRFU dismisses World Rugby suggestion to move Ireland Six Nations fixtures stateside
teams.body: The IRFU has rejected suggestions of moving Six Nations fixtures to the United States, insisting there are "currently no plans or discussions" regarding the proposal. The statement follows World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin's suggestion that an Ireland versus Italy clash would resonate with American fans. While acknowledging the US as a growth market, the union prioritised the tournament's traditional appeal for home supporters. The Italian Rugby Federation also distanced itself from the idea, despite having previously faced Ireland in Chicago back in 2018.

teams.heading: John Mitchell reveals stance on controversial WXV smaller ball trial impacting Scotland
teams.body: World Rugby’s trial of a smaller ball continues to cause debate as Scotland prepare for Saturday’s opener against Canada. Designed to improve handling and kicking, the move has been met with a “mixed bag of emotions” by players, with some suggesting the change makes technical skills more difficult. While England coach Mitchell has now weighed in on the controversy, the trial remains open until the governing body determines if the change becomes permanent following the conclusion of the current WXV tournament window.

teams.heading: Rhys Long returns to WRU with plan to overhaul talent pathway
teams.body: Reported this week, new Welsh Rugby Union technical director Rhys Long has returned from the English FA to restructure the nation’s talent development. Reporting to elite performance director Dave Reddin, Long aims to replace short-term rebuilding with a pathway focused on the next 15 years. Following Wales’ fall to ninth in the Nations Championship log, Long remains confident in the country’s raw potential. He told WalesOnline: “I wouldn’t have taken this job if I didn’t think we could put in place the talent development system that I know we’re capable of.”

teams.heading: Argentina halt three-match losing streak with Mendoza draw against Australia
teams.body: Argentina secured a 28-28 draw against Australia in Mendoza this month to end a difficult run of results, though the visitors clinched the series. In their last five games, the side has won one, lost three, and drawn one, with the sequence recorded as draw, loss, loss, loss, and win. This latest result followed three consecutive defeats for the national team. Within the Nations Championship standings, the side currently sits eighth after recording one win and two losses.

teams.heading: James Slipper pauses playing career to join Brumbies as scrum coach
teams.body: Veteran Wallabies prop James Slipper has been appointed as the Brumbies’ new scrum coach on a temporary basis. The 154-Test veteran, who recently extended his playing contract by one year, will focus on developing the club’s forwards during the Super Rugby AUS campaign. Slipper, the most experienced international prop in history, stated he is keen to pass on lessons from his extensive career. He joins head coach Stephen Larkham’s staff as the Brumbies prepare for their opening match against the Waratahs.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones targets cup glory as Japan hosts USA in Osaka
teams.body: Japan begins its Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup campaign today with a semi-final clash against the USA at Hanazono Rugby Stadium. Seeking to improve on consecutive runner-up finishes behind Fiji, the Brave Blossoms enter as favourites given their 12th-place world ranking compared to the USA’s 14th. While the historic head-to-head record remains tight, Japan has won 9 of the last 10 encounters. Head coach Eddie Jones is aiming to secure the title for the first time since 2019.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie names Richie Mo’unga for decisive Baltimore series finale
teams.body: Coach Dave Rennie has reshuffled his side for the fourth Test in Baltimore, headlined by the return of Richie Mo’unga at flyhalf. The All Blacks are looking to level the series after conceding back-to-back defeats in South Africa. Springbok assistant coach Mzwandile Stick acknowledged the selection, noting that the tourists will likely be "even more bold" in their attacking intent. With Anton Lienert-Brown also joining the midfield, New Zealand aim to recapture the momentum that saw them score 13 tries across the series.
